headline: Nasdaq-100 futures test the upper edge of their Sunday restart band as an Asian memory-chip rally meets a closed US cash session on Labor Day
body:
The observation that changed this hour is the top of the range. Investing.com's delayed feed puts NQ front-month at 29,640.25, up 75.00 points or 0.25%, while Yahoo's feed still shows 29,565.25; both sit inside a restart band whose high has extended from 29,622.75 to 29,643.00 since the last assessment. That band now runs 29,530.50 to 29,643.00, about 113 points or 0.38% wide, and has contained roughly nine hours of trade. A marginal new high with price near the extreme is one of the amplifiers that matters, so Tail lifts two points to 7. It stays deep inside the low band because the other three signatures are absent: pullbacks have been repeated rather than shallow, no retracement has failed and extended, and the total excursion over nine hours is well under half a percent.

The driver is identifiable and it is not a risk event. Asian technology rallied hard on OpenAI's Astra model release reviving the memory trade, with SK Hynix up about 6% and Samsung about 4% in Seoul; South Korea's index closed up 4.3% and Japan's Nikkei rebounded 2.0%, while Hong Kong fell about 1%. That follows Friday's US session in which semiconductors were broadly bid even as Apple, Microsoft and Tesla fell. A sector-rotation bid of this kind normally produces grind rather than the violent one-way repricing that denies mean reversion.

The energy and rates channels are the counterweight and neither deteriorated. WTI is quoted at $91.48 and Brent at $96.28, below the $92.57 and $97.37 that Reuters recorded near 05:57 UTC, so the weekend risk premium from the US-Iran tanker exchange in the Strait of Hormuz is still being given back rather than rebuilt. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.784%, near its highest since late 2023, and futures price a 58% probability of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September after August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with the unemployment rate at 4.1%. Those are Stress and Confidence inputs; they hold Stress at 54.

Today is a US holiday. Cash equity and Treasury markets are closed for Labor Day, CME equity index futures go to an early halt at 17:00 UTC and reopen at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date, and there is no scheduled US macro release. Conditional risk therefore concentrates in two narrow stretches rather than across the session: the 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the halt, and the 22:00 UTC restart. Confidence holds at 86 on two independent live futures feeds, verified crude and yield levels, a verified payrolls print and a verified event calendar; the shared Finviz context was more than five hours old at run time and was treated as stale.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, then eased to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly, and has stayed at 5 for the last seven available hours. Stress opened the window at 53, dipped to a 52 low at 07:00 UTC on 6 September, drifted up through a 54-58 band as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, peaked at 60 at 20:00 UTC, then eased through 57, 56, 55, 54, 54, 55, 55 and 54 after the reopen. Confidence held a narrow 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 7 for the current hour and the next two while price sits near the band high, 8 across the European mid and late morning where holiday-thinned depth and the weekend Hormuz headlines meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 7 easing to 6 through the holiday-thinned midday and notional US pre-open, 7 across the notional US morning, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and 8 in the final hour before the halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 through the five halted hours, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing through 7 and 6 back to the floor of 5 across the Asian session. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green. Stress runs a 51-58 band, highest into the halt and lowest while the venue is shut, and Confidence decays from 86 to 73 as the last observed price path ages.

forecastDetail.comment: NQ last printed 29,640.25 on Investing.com's delayed feed, up 0.25% and at the top of a restart band whose high extended from 29,622.75 to 29,643.00. That band is roughly 113 points or 0.38% wide and has now contained about nine hours of trade. A marginal new high is one amplifier, but repeated two-sided rotation inside so narrow a band is the opposite of the persistent one-way structure that overwhelms mean reversion, so Tail stays deep inside the low band at 7.

European cash equities open into a futures market sitting near its band high. The first checkpoint is whether 29,643.00 is cleared and held or faded back into the band; a fade would confirm the containment of the last nine hours, while a hold above would be the first genuine piece of Tail evidence. With US cash equity and Treasury markets closed for Labor Day, European depth is the only real order book today.

The European morning proper is where the weekend US-Iran exchange in the Strait of Hormuz meets real depth for the first time. Crude has been giving back part of its weekend premium overnight, WTI to $91.48 and Brent to $96.28 against the $92.57 and $97.37 printed near 05:57 UTC. Whether that giveback continues or reverses is the hour's main cross-asset question; Tail is unchanged at 7.

Tail steps to 8 for the European mid-morning, the stretch where holiday-thinned depth could let a move extend without the usual US cash counterparty and where a geopolitical headline would transmit fastest. The step reflects thinner books rather than any observed break of structure. A return into the middle of the restart band would invalidate the concern.

Conditional Tail holds at 8 with the drivers pointed against each other rather than aligned: an AI-memory bid supporting tech, an energy channel and a 10-year yield at 4.784% near its highest since late 2023 working the other way. Conflicting cross-asset signals of this kind lift Stress, which reaches its European-session peak of 57 here, well before they lift Tail.

Tail eases to 7 as the European morning matures and weekend-headline repricing is normally absorbed. The residual conditional risk is a late-morning extension that then fails to retrace, which is the specific signature that matters for a mean-reversion approach. Absent that, the band-bound pattern established over the last nine hours remains the base case into the holiday midday.
